subject: Lyginopteris supported scrambling gland-bearing seed fern
factual_scope: Lyginopteris oldhamia whole-habit hypothesis. Primary biomechanical abstract supports a prolonged semi-self-supporting growth phase and later scrambling; Seward original specimen figures support divided lobed foliage and glandular emergences. Dead support is explicit illustrative scene aid, not claimed fossil organ or second living organism. Overall size, exact arrangements, palette and count are art choices.
identifying_features: One slender non-twining leaning/scandent stem supported at a genuine contact by one subordinate dead forked twig. Six sparsely spaced divided fronds on stem, not a basal fern rosette.

Each frond divides into two fan arms, each with three pinnae bearing six small deeply lobed pinnules:216 pinnules total. Coherent leaf blades, petioles and branches are connected, not floating fan cutouts.

Twenty-four small scattered gland-base nubs on exposed axis, not oversized nodal bead bunches or microscopic hairs. Sterile specimen; associated Lagenostoma organs not separate assets and not modeled.
